key_insight: An LLM-driven evolutionary search can discover new fermion-to-qubit encodings with strictly higher verified distance and better qubit compression than prior GSE/superfast constructions for molecular simulation.
engineering_relevance: The paper suggests a practical design loop for quantum encoding synthesis: use an external verifier to keep error-correcting properties fixed while optimizing resource usage such as qubits per mode.
method: LLM edits constructor programs for the Generalized Superfast Encoding (GSE).
An external verifier scores candidates by exact stabilizer-coset distance and resource metrics.
High-scoring programs are retained, re-mutated, and refined into interpretable encoding rules.
evidence_signal: On tested molecular instances, the discovered codes achieved exact distance 5, with distance 6 on one 20-mode case, and a second search reached a five-qubits-per-mode floor on 12-, 14-, 16-, and 20-mode instances.
watch_item: The reported gains are for verified encoding properties and memory-style comparisons only; the abstract does not claim circuit-level fault tolerance or Trotter-cost improvements.
paper_title: Evolving Quantum Error-Correcting Encodings for Molecular Simulation
